sections.h2: Where does Bertie County record deeds, and what are the hours?
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded in Windsor, in the courthouse at King and Dundee streets, where the register's office occupies the first floor. Visitors use 108 Dundee Street; mail goes to PO Box 340, Windsor, NC 27983.

Staff are in from 8:30 to 5:00, but the recording cutoff is 4:30 every day, so a deed delivered at a quarter to five sits until the next morning. Electronic recording is accepted now, which lets a closing attorney send the deed without a drive to Windsor. Holidays and bad weather can close the doors.

sections.h2: What does the register keep, and why does recording matter?
sections.html:
The register looks after deeds, deeds of trust, powers of attorney, assumed names, plats, maps and military discharge papers. Voters pick the register every two years, and the office answers to Chapter 161 of the General Statutes.

Recording gives a buyer priority. Under G.S. 47-18, an unrecorded conveyance has no force against lien creditors or purchasers who paid value, and the order of registration sets who ranks first. Until the deed is filed in the county where the land lies, the buyer is exposed to a competing claim.

  • Records are filed by name, so the office cannot look up an owner from a street address.
  • For an address search, call the tax assessor's mapping line at (252) 794-5311.
  • Anyone may obtain copies of recorded papers in person, by mail or by phone request, except military discharge forms, which have limited access.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed in Bertie County cost?
sections.html:
The charges come from the uniform statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10, which the county reprints on its fee page. A standard instrument costs $26.00 and covers 15 pages, with $4.00 for every page past that. A deed of trust or mortgage costs $64.00 and covers 35 pages, then $4.00 a page.

  • An additional instrument inside the same document adds $10.00.
  • A non-standard document adds $25.00 on top of the recording fee.
  • A satisfaction or cancellation of a mortgage is recorded free.
  • A plat costs $21.00 a sheet, and a certified copy costs $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each added page.

The statute describes the schedule as complete and exclusive, so no other filing charge applies, and payment is due before filing. Call the office at (252) 794-5309 for a document with an unusual page count.

sections.h2: Who pays the transfer tax on a Bertie County deed?
sections.html:
The seller pays. State law taxes every conveyance of real property at $1.00 for each $500 of price or value, counting any leftover fraction of $500 as a full unit, and the transferor delivers the money to the register before the deed goes on record.

The county keeps half of it for the general fund. The other half, minus refunds and the county's allowance, goes to the Department of Revenue every month. If a tract straddles two counties, the county with the larger share of the value collects the tax.

Your closing attorney will work out the exact figure from the price on the settlement statement, and the rounding rule for each $500 can move it.

sections.h2: What do Bertie County's own recording rules require?
sections.html:
A resolution adopted in April 1991 under G.S. 161-30 took effect June 1, 1991. It bars the register from accepting any map or instrument affecting real property unless two items appear on its face: the name and address of the person who should get the document back, and the grantee's permanent mailing address.

Statewide format rules also apply, and the office posts them for filers. The paper must be 8-1/2 by 11 or 8-1/2 by 14. The first page needs a 3 inch blank top margin and half inch margins elsewhere, with every later page at half inch all around. Text must be black on white, 9 point or larger, printed on one side, and the type of instrument goes at the top of page one below the margin.

A paper that misses the format is recorded after the $25.00 non-standard fee. The register may waive that fee when the type is a bit small but still legible.

  • Return name and address on the first page
  • Grantee's permanent mailing address on the first page
  • Margins, font size and one-sided printing checked
  • Deed signed and notarized

sections.h2: How are names changed on a Bertie County deed?
sections.html:
A new deed has to be drawn up, and the register's FAQ sends owners to an attorney for it. After signing and notarization, the deed is brought to the office with the fee.

A land contract works differently. Under Chapter 47H, the seller must record the contract, or a short memorandum of it, within five business days, and the purchaser can cancel until midnight of the third business day after signing.

Paid-off loans leave a loose end. Ask the lender for a satisfaction and have it recorded, which costs nothing and clears the title check before a sale.

sections.h2: How does the register fit into a Bertie County sale?
sections.html:
The closing attorney or title agent searches the records, files the new deed and any new deed of trust, and pays the transfer tax from the settlement. Most sellers never visit the office themselves. Census QuickFacts counts 9,116 housing units in the county as of July 2025, and every one of those deeds is filed at this single courthouse office on Dundee Street.

Property taxes are the one title item that lives elsewhere. Unpaid bills are a lien and are cleared with the tax collector, as covered in our Bertie County property tax guide. Gaps from older paperwork, such as a mortgage never released or an estate never opened, get fixed by recording the missing document before closing.

faqs.q: What is the Bertie County Register of Deeds phone number?
faqs.a: Call (252) 794-5309. The fax is (252) 794-5374, and the office is at 108 Dundee Street in Windsor.

faqs.q: How late can I record a deed in Bertie County?
faqs.a: Recording ends at 4:30 p.m. each day, even though the office stays open until 5:00 p.m. Electronic recording is also accepted.

faqs.q: What does a standard deed cost to record in Bertie County?
faqs.a: A standard instrument costs $26.00 for up to 15 pages, then $4.00 for each added page. A deed of trust costs $64.00 for up to 35 pages. Non-standard format adds $25.00.

faqs.q: Who owes the deed tax on a Bertie County sale?
faqs.a: The seller owes it, at $1.00 per $500 of value, paid to the register before recording.

faqs.q: Can the register tell me who owns a Bertie County address?
faqs.a: No. Records are kept by name, so call the tax assessor's mapping office at (252) 794-5311 with the address.
